meta.title_tag: Six weeks of warning on a 13bn euro deal
meta.headline: Our partners were briefed on a €13bn takeover six weeks before the market called it.
meta.sub: Uber's bid for Delivery Hero broke on 15 July 2026. Most of the individual signals were public and easy to miss. We sequenced the behavioural pattern, the hiring, the positioning and the market reaction, to work out what was coming and roughly when.
meta.forming_head: What was forming, and when the work lands
meta.lead: Named individuals and direct email addresses were supplied to partners on 2 June. Redacted here.
meta.strap: We did not break this story. We assembled it.

events.text: Delivery Hero hires a senior antitrust and trade lawyer
First reports Uber is studying a full takeover
Uber weighs raising its offer; shares climb 10%
An antitrust hire alongside takeover chatter is a preparation pattern. We sequenced it and gave partners the angle and the window
Structure narrows to the regional businesses

Uber bids €41.50 a share,
valuing Delivery Hero near €13bn

steps.head: We found it
steps.body: A senior antitrust and trade lawyer hired in Berlin. On its own, an ordinary vacancy. Nobody was reading it as a deal signal.

steps.head: We sequenced it
steps.body: The hire, the takeover reports and the market reaction held together as one situation, not five unrelated stories.

steps.head: We told you
steps.body: On the board with the evidence, the reason it mattered now, and the window before the market repriced it.

meta.title_tag: Five weeks ahead of a 5.7bn take-private
meta.headline: We tracked a £5.7bn take-private from first rumour to final bid.
meta.sub: Castlelake's interest in easyJet surfaced on 30 May 2026. It was on our board the next day. We read the behaviour, not the headline: a rejected approach that keeps returning with a higher number is a pattern we track, and it told us terms were coming well before they did.
meta.forming_head: What was forming, and when the work lands
meta.lead: Named individuals and direct email addresses were supplied to partners on 31 May. Redacted here.
meta.strap: Four rejections. Two bidders. One sequence.

events.text: A US private credit firm is reported to be circling
An opportunistic approach into a depressed share price, the profile that historically precedes a repeat bidder. On the board next morning
easyJet calls the timing opportunistic; shares jump 10%
A second suitor is reported to be interested
Third proposal rejected; bidder goes direct to shareholders

Board agrees terms.
Rival bid follows at £5.7bn

steps.head: We found it
steps.body: A US private credit firm circling a depressed UK airline. Reported once, then largely dropped by the market.

steps.head: We sequenced it
steps.body: An opportunistic approach into a weak share price is a profile that historically precedes a repeat bidder, so we tracked the escalation rather than the headline.

steps.head: We told you
steps.body: On the board the next morning at confidence 65, lifted to 88 as the bidder returned twice more and a second suitor appeared.

meta.title_tag: Five weeks inside Europe's biggest bank fight
meta.headline: We had partners inside the €39bn bank fight five weeks before its endgame.
meta.sub: A public rebuff, a regulator complaint, a government rejection, and the stake rising anyway. We sequenced the behaviour, not the headlines. An acquirer that keeps buying through every obstacle is telling you how this ends, months before the market prices it.
meta.forming_head: What was forming, and when the work lands
meta.lead: Named individuals and direct email addresses were supplied to partners on 2 June. Redacted here.
meta.strap: Nobody missed the deal. Everybody missed the build-up.

events.text: Commerzbank's chief executive publicly rebuffs the approach
Rebuffed in public yet still accumulating stock. That behaviour rarely reverses, so we surfaced it at confidence 88
The bank contacts the German regulator over the stake build
Berlin rejects the €39bn approach outright
The stake is lifted to 42.5% regardless

Control nears.
Institutions accept.

steps.head: We found it
steps.body: A chief executive publicly rebuffing an approach. Read as a defence, it looks like the end of a story rather than the start of one.

steps.head: We sequenced it
steps.body: The rebuff, the regulator complaint, the government rejection and a rising stake are one behaviour, not four events. An acquirer buying through every obstacle has already decided.

steps.head: We told you
steps.body: Surfaced at confidence 88 as a live situation rather than a rumour, with work identified for both sides regardless of who prevailed.

meta.title_tag: A withdrawn bid read as the start, not the end
meta.headline: A bidder walked away from Bodycote. We read that as the opening, not the close.
meta.sub: Apollo pulled a £1.5bn approach on 8 June and the market filed it as a story that ended. A withdrawn bid is the one public confirmation that a board has seen a price and refused it. Eighty-five days later a contested process settled at 940 pence.
meta.forming_head: What was forming, and when the work lands
meta.lead: Named individuals and direct email addresses were supplied to partners on 28 July. Redacted here.
meta.strap: We did not break this story. We assembled it.

events.text: Apollo withdraws a £1.5bn approach for Bodycote
First-half growth reported alongside a streamlining plan
A withdrawn bid alongside self-help restructuring is a board defending a valuation it has already been shown. Surfaced at confidence 90
Twin private equity bids land on the board

Veritas Capital wins the board recommendation
at 940 pence, with CVC still in the room

steps.head: We found it
steps.body: A withdrawn approach, filed by most readers as a story that ended. It is the only public proof that a board has been shown a number and turned it down.

steps.head: We sequenced it
steps.body: The withdrawal, the streamlining plan and the twin bids are one situation held together, not three unrelated items about a heat-treatment group.

steps.head: We told you
steps.body: On the board at confidence 90 with the evidence and the window, before a contested process priced it at a 940 pence recommendation.

meta.title_tag: The seller of 70 theatres, named 82 days out
meta.headline: We named the seller of ATG's 70 theatres eighty-two days out.
meta.sub: On 21 May we recorded Providence Equity Partners preparing ATG Entertainment for a sale above £4bn. Right seller, right scale, right outcome. On 11 August Ariel Emanuel's MARI agreed to buy the business, an estate spanning the UK, US, Germany and Spain.
meta.forming_head: What was forming, and when the work lands
meta.lead: Named individuals and direct email addresses were supplied to partners on 21 May. Redacted here.
meta.strap: We did not break this story. We assembled it.

events.text: Providence preparing ATG for a potential sale above £4bn
A sponsor readying a 70-venue estate is an exit with a calendar, not a rumour. Surfaced with the seller named and the scale stated

MARI acquires ATG Entertainment
and its 70 venues from Providence

steps.head: We found it
steps.body: Sale preparation reported in trade press and read by almost nobody outside it. On its own, an ordinary item about a theatre operator.

steps.head: We sequenced it
steps.body: Held against the sponsor's hold period and the size of the estate, so the item read as a dated process rather than a possibility.

steps.head: We told you
steps.body: Seller named and scale stated, with the work identified for both sides, eleven weeks before a buyer was public.

meta.title_tag: Four filings that only make sense during a live bid
meta.headline: Four disclosures at Gamma that only make sense during a live bid.
meta.sub: A Takeover Panel extension, a buyback during an offer period, a second extension, and an institutional Form 8.3. Each one ordinary alone; together, a process running to a clock. On 1 September Epiris agreed a £1.0bn take-private at a 53% premium.
meta.forming_head: What was forming, and when the work lands
meta.lead: Named individuals and direct email addresses were supplied to partners on 9 July. Redacted here.
meta.strap: We did not break this story. We assembled it.

events.text: Takeover Panel extends the deadline for Epiris to make a formal offer
A bidder granted more time is a bidder still working. Extensions mean a deal being negotiated, not abandoned
Share buyback runs during an active offer period
Deadline extended again; BlackRock files Form 8.3

Epiris agrees a £1.0bn take-private
at a 53% premium

steps.head: We found it
steps.body: A procedural notice about a mid-cap telecoms provider. Read as administration, it looks like nothing at all.

steps.head: We sequenced it
steps.body: Four filings held together as one situation. A company does not buy back its own shares mid-offer unless the board has a view on the price.

steps.head: We told you
steps.body: Bidder named and the Code timetable stated, so the approach could be made while the price was still being argued.

meta.title_tag: The bidder and the exact price, 23 days out
meta.headline: We named the bidder and the exact price at Pinewood twenty-three days out.
meta.sub: On 27 July we recorded a £545m proposal from Ridgeview for the UK automotive software provider. Same bidder, same figure, before the board had responded. On 19 August Ridgeview agreed a £545m take-private at a 43% premium, with Lithia locked up.
meta.forming_head: What was forming, and when the work lands
meta.lead: Named individuals and direct email addresses were supplied to partners on 27 July. Redacted here.
meta.strap: We did not break this story. We assembled it.

events.text: Ridgeview makes a £545m acquisition proposal for Pinewood
A named bidder at a named figure, with a majority holder on the register. The outcome turns on one shareholder, not on the market

Ridgeview agrees £545m at a 43% premium,
with Lithia locked up

steps.head: We found it
steps.body: A proposal reported at a specific figure, before the board had responded and before any terms were agreed.

steps.head: We sequenced it
steps.body: With a majority shareholder on the register, the outcome turns on a single decision. That narrows a public process to one conversation.

steps.head: We told you
steps.body: Bidder and price on the board before agreement, with the lock-up identified as the thing that would settle it.
